title: NIST AI RMF Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructure Profile Concept Note
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: NIST's concept note launches development of an AI Risk Management Framework profile for AI used across critical-infrastructure IT, operational technology, and industrial control systems.
key_findings: The proposed profile is intended to translate AI RMF trustworthiness characteristics into risk-management practices for critical-infrastructure operators, developers, and supply-chain participants.

The note emphasizes deterministic behavior, explainability, graceful degradation, fail-safe operation, adversarial robustness, rigorous testing, evaluation, validation, and verification, and supply-chain visibility.

Examples include AI-enabled plant monitoring, autonomous cyber response, diagnostic assistants, industrial robots and vehicles, data-center digital twins, and optimization systems with human oversight.
why_it_matters: The concept defines a concrete governance and assurance agenda for AI entering high-consequence physical systems, where generic AI-risk language is insufficient.
ftfn_relevance: Connects AI for Science, cybersecurity, infrastructure, manufacturing, mobility, and energy evidence lanes.
Names assurance properties that later standards, procurement, testbed, and deployment records should make inspectable.
Creates a watch rail for a future sector-spanning profile and associated implementation resources.
evidence_limits: This is a concept note for an ongoing profile-development process, not final guidance.
It does not create a binding requirement or prove adoption by critical-infrastructure operators.
Illustrative use cases do not establish deployed capability, safety, or performance.
